questions.stem:
A curve $C$ has equation
$y=\mathrm{e}^{2x}\tan x, \quad x \neq (2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2}$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that the turning points on $C$ occur where $\tan x=-1$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $\frac{dy}{dx}=2\mathrm{e}^{2x}\tan x+\mathrm{e}^{2x}\sec^2 x$ M1 A1+A1
$\frac{dy}{dx}=0 \Rightarrow 2\mathrm{e}^{2x}\tan x+\mathrm{e}^{2x}\sec^2 x=0$ M1
$2\tan x+1+\tan^2 x=0$ A1
$(\tan x+1)^2=0$
$\tan x=-1$ A1* cso

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find an equation of the tangent to $C$ at the point where $x=0$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)_0=1$ M1
Equation of tangent at $(0,0)$ is $y=x$ A1

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that there is a root of $\mathrm{f}(x)=0$ in the interval $2<x<3$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:

$\mathrm{f}(3)=-0.39…$
Change of sign (and continuity) $\Rightarrow$ root in $(2,3)$* cso A1

to calculate the values of $x_1, x_2$ and $x_3$ giving your answers to 5 decimal places.

questions.stem:
The radioactive decay of a substance is given by
$R=1000\mathrm{e}^{-ct}, \quad t \geqslant 0.$
where $R$ is the number of atoms at time $t$ years and $c$ is a positive constant.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the number of atoms when the substance started to decay.
(1)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
It takes 5730 years for half of the substance to decay.
(b) Find the value of $c$ to 3 significant figures.
(4)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Calculate the number of atoms that will be left when $t=22\,920$.
(2)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) In the space provided on page 13, sketch the graph of $R$ against $t$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme: (d) Shape B1; 1000 B1

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Use the double angle formulae and the identity
$\cos(A+B) \equiv \cos A \cos B - \sin A \sin B$
to obtain an expression for $\cos 3x$ in terms of powers of $\cos x$ only.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $\cos(2x+x)=\cos 2x \cos x - \sin 2x \sin x$ M1
$=(2\cos^2 x - 1)\cos x - (2\sin x \cos x)\sin x$ M1
$=(2\cos^2 x - 1)\cos x - 2(1-\cos^2 x)\cos x$ any correct expression A1
$=4\cos^3 x - 3\cos x$ A1

parts.label: b(i)
parts.text:
(b) (i) Prove that
$\frac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}+\frac{1+\sin x}{\cos x} \equiv 2\sec x, \quad x \neq (2n+1)\frac{\pi}{2}.$
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b)(i) $\frac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}+\frac{1+\sin x}{\cos x}=\frac{\cos^2 x+(1+\sin x)^2}{(1+\sin x)\cos x}$ M1
$=\frac{\cos^2 x+1+2\sin x+\sin^2 x}{(1+\sin x)\cos x}$ A1
$=\frac{2(1+\sin x)}{(1+\sin x)\cos x}$ M1
$=\frac{2}{\cos x}=2\sec x$* cso A1

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.text:
(ii) Hence find, for $0<x<2\pi$, all the solutions of
$\frac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}+\frac{1+\sin x}{\cos x}=4.$
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(ii) $\sec x=2$ or $\cos x=\frac{1}{2}$ M1
$x=\frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{5\pi}{3}$ accept awrt 1.05, 5.24 A1, A1

questions.stem:
A curve $C$ has equation
$y=3\sin 2x+4\cos 2x, \quad -\pi \leqslant x \leqslant \pi.$
The point $A(0, 4)$ lies on $C$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find an equation of the normal to the curve $C$ at $A$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $\frac{dy}{dx}=6\cos 2x - 8\sin 2x$ M1 A1
$\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)_0=6$ B1
$y-4=-\frac{1}{6}x$ or equivalent M1 A1

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Express $y$ in the form $R\sin(2x+\alpha)$, where $R>0$ and $0<\alpha<\frac{\pi}{2}$.
Give the value of $\alpha$ to 3 significant figures.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $R=\sqrt{(3^2+4^2)}=5$ M1 A1
$\tan \alpha=\frac{4}{3}$, $\alpha \approx 0.927$ awrt 0.927 M1 A1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the coordinates of the points of intersection of the curve $C$ with the $x$-axis.
Give your answers to 2 decimal places.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $\sin(2x+\text{their }\alpha)=0$ M1
$x=-2.03, -0.46, 1.11, 2.68$ A1 A1 A1
First A1 any correct solution; second A1 a second correct solution; third A1 all four correct and to the specified accuracy or better.
Ignore the $y$-coordinate.

questions.stem:
The functions f and g are defined by
$\mathrm{f}:x \mapsto 1-2x^3, \quad x \in \mathbb{R}$
$\mathrm{g}:x \mapsto \frac{3}{x}-4, \quad x>0, \quad x \in \mathbb{R}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the inverse function $\mathrm{f}^{-1}$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $x=1-2y^3 \Rightarrow y=\left(\frac{1-x}{2}\right)^{1/3}$ or $\sqrt[3]{\frac{1-x}{2}}$ M1 A1
$\mathrm{f}^{-1}:x \mapsto \left(\frac{1-x}{2}\right)^{1/3}$ Ignore domain

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Show that the composite function gf is
$\mathrm{gf}:x \mapsto \frac{8x^3-1}{1-2x^3}.$
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\mathrm{gf}(x)=\frac{3}{1-2x^3}-4$ M1 A1
$=\frac{3-4(1-2x^3)}{1-2x^3}$ M1
$=\frac{8x^3-1}{1-2x^3}$* cso A1
$\mathrm{gf}:x \mapsto \frac{8x^3-1}{1-2x^3}$ Ignore domain

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Solve $\mathrm{gf}(x)=0$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $8x^3-1=0$ Attempting solution of numerator $=0$ M1
$x=\frac{1}{2}$ Correct answer and no additional answers A1

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Use calculus to find the coordinates of the stationary point on the graph of $y=\mathrm{gf}(x)$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{(1-2x^3)\times 24x^2+(8x^3-1)\times 6x^2}{(1-2x^3)^2}$ M1 A1
$=\frac{18x^2}{(1-2x^3)^2}$ A1
Solving their numerator $=0$ and substituting to find $y$. M1
$x=0, y=-1$ A1
